Traditional crop rotation customs in Upper Egypt have modified agricultural regulations
Emergency food security provisions allow temporary import of normally restricted agricultural goods
laws.sourceLabel: Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

quiz.q: Why did Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine create a food security emergency in Egypt?
options: Russia directly blockaded Egypt as part of international pressure on Western allies
Egypt imported 60-70% of its wheat from Russia and Ukraine — the war disrupted supply and raised prices dramatically, threatening Egypt's bread subsidy and food security
Ukraine produced Egypt's entire sugar crop — the war ended sugar imports
Egypt was unaffected by Ukraine war because it grows all its own food
quiz.explanation: Egypt — the world's largest wheat importer — sourced approximately 60-70% of its wheat from Russia and Ukraine before the 2022 invasion. Russia's blockade of Ukrainian Black Sea ports and disruption of supply chains caused immediate wheat price spikes globally, but was particularly devastating for Egypt: it directly threatened the country's bread subsidy program that feeds 60M+ people. Egypt scrambled to find alternative suppliers (Romania, Australia, France) and used strategic reserves. The crisis exposed Egypt's dangerous food import dependence on a single volatile region and accelerated discussions about agricultural self-sufficiency.

laws.title: Egyptian Drug Regulatory Authority and Pharma Sector
laws.subtitle: Egypt's pharmaceutical industry and medicine regulation
laws.fullDescription: Egypt's Drug Regulatory Authority (EDRA) regulates medicines and medical devices. Egypt has a significant domestic pharmaceutical sector: 130+ companies producing 90%+ of medicines domestically. Egypt is a major pharmaceutical exporter in Africa and Arab world. Egypt's Hepatitis C treatment program (2014-2019) was a global health success: Egypt had the world's highest Hepatitis C prevalence (15-20% of adults, from 1960s-1980s government anti-schistosomiasis injection campaigns using unsterilized needles). The Egyptian government negotiated a special deal with Gilead Sciences for generic sofosbuvir at $100 per 12-week course (vs. $1,000/pill in US). Egypt treated 4M+ patients — achieving Hepatitis C cure rates above 90% and dramatically reducing prevalence.
laws.penalty: Counterfeit medicines: up to 10 years imprisonment. Practicing pharmacy without license: up to 2 years. Importing unregistered medicines: administrative confiscation and criminal prosecution.
exceptions: Clinical trial medicines under international protocols may be imported without standard EDRA registration
Emergency medicines during health crises may be imported under expedited authorization
Diplomatic and international organizations may import personal prescription medicines without Egyptian registration

quiz.q: How did Egypt achieve one of the world's biggest Hepatitis C treatment success stories?
options: Egypt discovered a new cure for Hepatitis C using ancient pharaonic herbal remedies

Egypt negotiated a deal with Gilead Sciences for generic sofosbuvir at $100/course (vs. $1,000/pill in US) and treated 4M+ patients — dramatically reducing one of the world's highest Hepatitis C prevalence rates
Egypt received free Hepatitis C medicines from the WHO worth $10B
Egypt eliminated Hepatitis C by quarantining all infected patients
quiz.explanation: Egypt's Hepatitis C treatment program is a global public health landmark. Egypt had the world's highest Hepatitis C prevalence (15-20% of adults) because of 1960s-80s mass injection campaigns for schistosomiasis using unsterilized needles. When sofosbuvir (a highly effective cure) became available, Egypt negotiated one of the world's lowest prices through competitive generic licensing and a bulk purchase agreement. By treating 4M+ patients at $100/course, Egypt reduced Hepatitis C prevalence from 15-20% to under 5%. The program is studied globally as a model for making expensive medicines affordable for large treatment programs in developing countries.

laws.title: Egypt Social Media Law and Political Control
laws.subtitle: How Egypt uses digital surveillance to control political space
laws.fullDescription: Egypt's government monitors social media extensively: dedicated units track Twitter, Facebook, TikTok, and WhatsApp groups. Egypt has arrested 1,000+ people for social media posts since 2013 — from tweeting criticism of el-Sisi to posting videos of protests. The Cybercrime Law (2018) criminalizes content 'threatening national security' and allows blocking websites. Egypt blocks 500+ websites including news sites, VPN services, and human rights organizations. Egypt uses surveillance technology (acquired from European vendors) for targeted monitoring. TikTok stars have been arrested for 'promoting debauchery' (content deemed morally inappropriate). Egypt ranks 'Not Free' on Freedom House Internet Freedom Index.
laws.penalty: Social media post threatening national security: up to 2 years. Publishing false news that disrupts national peace: up to 1 year. 'Debauchery' through social media: 6 months to 1 year.
exceptions: State media and licensed news organizations may publish within approved parameters
Academic institutions analyzing social media for research have some protection
Government officials may use social media to promote official positions without restriction
laws.sourceLabel: Egyptian Ministry of Communications and Information Technology

quiz.q: How many websites has Egypt blocked, and what kinds of content are targeted?
options: Egypt blocks 5 websites — primarily terrorist recruitment sites
Egypt has blocked 500+ websites including news sites, VPN services, human rights organizations, and political opposition platforms — ranking 'Not Free' on internet freedom indices
Egypt has blocked only foreign pornography websites — domestic content is unrestricted
Egypt has no internet censorship — it is a completely open internet country
quiz.explanation: Egypt has blocked over 500 websites since 2017, when the government began systematic internet censorship. Blocked sites include: independent news outlets (Mada Masr, Buzzfeed Arabic, Daily News Egypt), international media critical of Egypt (Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye), human rights organizations, VPN services that circumvent blocks, and opposition political platforms. Egypt uses Deep Packet Inspection technology to identify and block content. The Committee to Protect Journalists and Freedom House consistently rate Egypt's internet environment as 'Not Free'. The blocks are so extensive that many journalists and civil society workers in Egypt use VPNs daily despite their technical illegality.

laws.title: Egyptian Judiciary — Constitutional Court and Independence
laws.subtitle: Egypt's constitutional court vs. executive power
laws.fullDescription: Egypt's Constitutional Court has demonstrated independence in notable cases: it dissolved Parliament in 2012 (Islamist-dominated) and again in 2013 (on procedural grounds). These dissolutions contributed to political instability. Under el-Sisi, judicial independence has been reduced: el-Sisi's government changed rules for appointing constitutional court justices, giving the president more control; State Security Prosecution (a specialized security-focused prosecution) handles sensitive cases; and the Emergency Supreme State Security Courts bypass normal judicial procedures. Despite constraints, Egyptian judges have occasionally issued independent judgments. The 2019 constitutional amendment gave the president power to nominate the heads of independent judicial bodies.
laws.penalty: Judicial corruption: up to 10 years imprisonment. Contempt of court: up to 6 months. Bribery of judge: up to 10 years.
exceptions: Constitutional Court decisions have binding effect on all courts and authorities — the strongest judicial protection
Supreme Administrative Court (Conseil d'État model) provides check on executive administrative decisions
Cassation Court reviews decisions of lower courts on points of law

quiz.q: What dramatic judicial action did Egypt's Constitutional Court take in 2012 that affected political stability?
options: The Constitutional Court upheld all elected institutions — showing complete judicial deference to democracy
The Court dissolved the Islamist-dominated Parliament in 2012 on constitutional grounds — contributing to political instability during Egypt's fragile democratic transition
The Court declared el-Sisi's 2013 coup unconstitutional but was overruled by the military
The Constitutional Court was dissolved itself — by the Muslim Brotherhood government
quiz.explanation: Egypt's Supreme Constitutional Court issued a landmark ruling in June 2012 dissolving the People's Assembly (Parliament) elected after the 2011 revolution — finding the electoral law unconstitutional because it allowed political parties to compete for seats reserved for independents. The timing was explosive: it came just weeks before Mohamed Morsi's presidential inauguration. The military (SCAF) had already expanded its powers. The parliamentary dissolution left Egypt without a legislature during the transition, and Morsi subsequently tried to reconvene Parliament before the Court confirmed its dissolution. The judicial actions were part of an intensely contested power struggle between military, judiciary, and Islamists.
